LSE 0.5.0 makes the engine something you can embed: the whole engine is now a library with a plain C API, it runs inside an iPad app driving an external AMD GPU, and it can tell you what a model is and how much device memory a configuration needs before you load anything.

## Highlights

1. **libLSE, the engine in process.** [`include/lse/lse.h`](https://github.com/Geramy/LSE/blob/v0.5.0/include/lse/lse.h) is a plain C API built on every platform: `lse_open` loads a model, `lse_request` takes the same OpenAI-shaped JSON the HTTP server does and answers through a callback (whole or streamed), `lse_cancel` stops a request, `lse_status` reports load progress, counters, timings and the device memory held, and `lse_http_start` optionally serves the same engine over HTTP. `lse-server` is now a thin command line over this library, and both transports give identical answers. Swift imports it directly.

2. **iOS and iPadOS.** An M-series iPad runs Qwen3.8-27B on an AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 over Thunderbolt, with [mac_linuxgpu](https://github.com/lemonade-sdk/mac_linuxgpu)'s driver embedded in the app and LSE linked as `LSE.xcframework` (libLSE, HRX, Loom, the tokenizer and the static HSA runtime, exporting only the `lse_*` API). Kernels are generated on the device and cached in the app's `Library/Caches`. Measured on an iPad Pro (M4), Qwen3.8-27B Q4 with the Q8 DFlash2 draft, warm:

   | | iPad Pro (M4), v0.5.0 | MacBook Pro (M5 Max), v0.4.24 |
   | --- | ---: | ---: |
   | Decode | **40.5 tok/s** at 73% draft acceptance | 43.3 tok/s at 74% |
   | Decode at 85–93% acceptance | **57–70 tok/s** | |
   | Model load | about 34 s | |
   | Operations that fell back to the CPU | **0** | 0 |

   At similar draft acceptance (73% against 74%) the iPad decodes within 7% of the Mac.

3. **DFlash2 takes the BF16 checkpoint directly.** `--dflash2-model` now accepts the original BF16 DFlash2 checkpoint, as a directory or a Hugging Face repository ID. LSE converts it to affine Q8/group64 once (bit-identical to `scripts/convert_dflash2_q8.py`, streaming, a few MiB of memory), caches the result beside the source or under `$LSE_DFLASH2_CACHE_DIR`, and loads the cached copy from then on. `LSE_DFLASH2_AUTOCONVERT=0` loads a BF16 draft unconverted.

4. **Model info and memory estimates without loading.** `lse_model_info` (and `lse-server --model-info`) describes a checkpoint from its `config.json` and tensor headers in milliseconds, with no device: the architecture LSE detects from the tensor names, dense or MoE, widths, which layers hold KV and which are linear-attention layers, context limits, quantization, bytes on disk and in VRAM, MTP and DFlash2 facts, and KV bytes per token for `fp32`, `fp16`, `bf16`, `fp8` and `bf8`. `lse_estimate` (and `--estimate`) takes the settings `lse_open` would take and reports the device memory that load would use, by component, plus the longest `--kv-len` that fits a memory budget. Weights, KV, recurrent state, RoPE tables and the DFlash2 ring follow the engine's own allocation rules: loading Qwen3.8-27B Q4 with its Q8 DFlash2 or MTP draft on the host backend matches the estimate to within 0.001%, and KV pools match to the byte. Activation and workspace are modelled and marked approximate; for a 68,301-token Q4 + DFlash2 context the estimate gives 27.73 GB against 27.83 GB measured on an R9700.

## Also in this release

- `GET /v1/models` reports the loaded model's `context_length`, `kv_len`, `kv_cache_dtype` and draft.
- A running server answers `GET /v1/lse/model_info` and `GET`/`POST /v1/lse/estimate` for the model it loaded, so a client can size a restart with other settings. A server never inspects a path a client names.
- `lse_status` and `/v1/lse/estimate` report the device bytes the engine currently holds and their peak.

## Downloads

| Asset | For |
| --- | --- |
| `lse-v0.5.0-macos-arm64.tar.gz` | macOS 15+ on Apple Silicon with an external AMD GPU and the [mac_linuxgpu](https://github.com/lemonade-sdk/mac_linuxgpu) driver |
| `lse-v0.5.0-ios-arm64.xcframework.zip` | iOS/iPadOS 26+ apps that embed the mac_linuxgpu driver; contains `LSE.xcframework` |
| `lse-v0.5.0-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` | Linux x86_64 with ROCm 7.x |

Each asset has a `.sha256` beside it. Check it with `shasum -a 256 -c` (macOS) or `sha256sum -c` (Linux) before you extract.

## Upgrading

- The C ABI version is unchanged (`LSE_ABI_VERSION` 1); 0.5.0 adds functions and changes no existing structure.
- The macOS package still uses the HSA runtime the GPU driver installs and does not bundle one. Install or update [mac_linuxgpu](https://github.com/lemonade-sdk/mac_linuxgpu) first.
- Kernel cache entries carry the engine version, so the first launch after updating compiles kernels again; later launches reuse them.
